story: Gary is at home on a sunny Friday morning, testing the light strings and speakers on his golf cart at low volume to make sure the wiring holds up. Over on Magnolia Loop, Hal is dutifully counting Donna's flamingos against the three-ornament limit, since Donna has promised there are exactly three. Donna, cheerful as ever, has reminded Hal that they'll meet at Rosa's at six, and she's bringing her deviled eggs. Rosa, content in her kitchen, is getting the sides and dessert going before turning the marinating dish.
events: Gary (gary golf cart): Test the light strings and speakers at low volume to make sure the wiring works
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street against the three-ornament limit
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Get the sides and dessert going, then turn the marinating dish

gary.thought_process: The lights and speaker wiring are mounted and hooked up to the battery. Before I call it done, I should test the whole rig. Lights are fine in daytime (Thanksgiving is coming, and L-04 covers lighting from then anyway), and a quick low-volume test of the speakers is well within the rules since it's 11 AM and quiet hours don't apply. The cart mods are already filed with Hal, so I'm legit. Nobody's around, so I can fiddle in peace, which is how I like it, though the house is quiet. Friday dinner with Donna and Rosa tonight gives me something to look forward to.

parameters.content: Test the light strings and speakers at low volume to make sure the wiring works

donna.thought_process: I'm back on Magnolia Loop after packing the bag and checking the calendar. Gary's court time is tomorrow at ten and dinner at Rosa's is Friday at six, so there's no rush on either. Hal is right here, and he's the one keeping the flamingo count honest. I've already pulled the extras behind the hedge, so I can invite him to look at the flock and confirm three, which keeps the committee happy and keeps me in good standing with the whole street. Plus I can remind him about dinner and spread a little goodwill.

parameters.content: Morning, Hal! Go ahead and count the flamingos from the street. Exactly three, I promise. See you at Rosa's at six, and I'm bringing my deviled eggs.

hal.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop with Donna just arrived beside her flamingo flock. L-02 caps ornaments at three visible from the street, so a count is exactly what I came for. I already logged one at tick 374, and the flock object is right here. I could fuss at her, but Friday dinner at Rosa's is tonight and I'd rather get a straight count than start a fight. Best move: interact with the flock and do an honest, by-the-book count, then talk to her with facts in hand.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street against the three-ornament limit

rosa.thought_process: It's 11:17 AM and I'm alone in the house. The main dish is marinating and the table is set for four. Last tick I was getting the sides and dessert started, so the kitchen is where I should be. Dinner's tonight, and I've got a shift schedule to keep straight too, but food comes first. Let me keep working: check the marinade, get the sides going, and pull dessert together so I'm not scrambling at five.

parameters.content: Get the sides and dessert going, then turn the marinating dish

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
